reasoning:
Analyzing FairTix's automation landscape reveals a ticketing platform that positions itself as the anti-bot, fair alternative to traditional ticketing monopolies. The company operates a lottery-based 'Fair Queue' system where customers enter draws for high-demand tickets rather than competing in bot-dominated first-come-first-served sales. Their value proposition centers on transparency (no hidden fees), fairness (resale price caps), and human verification.

Applying the five analytical methods:

1. CAPABILITY ENUMERATION: The lottery winner notification function is served by 3 nearly identical workflows, indicating significant drift/duplication. Customer support is handled by 3 overlapping AI-powered triage systems with different data sources (Gmail vs Sheets) but similar classification logic.

2. DEPENDENCY GRAPH: Gmail is critical - 7/8 workflows depend on it. Google Sheets serves as the primary database (5/8 workflows). Anthropic Claude powers all support automation (3 workflows). If Gmail credentials fail, most business processes stop. If Claude API fails, all support automation breaks.

3. DOMAIN-COVERAGE VERIFICATION: The workflows reference several domains with no corresponding automation: payment processing (mentioned in support categories), account verification (support category), resale/transfer management (support category), and the core Fair Queue algorithm itself (results appear in sheets but no workflow manages the lottery).

4. OPERATIONAL COHERENCE: Critical inconsistency - all customer-facing workflows are inactive despite being production-ready (based on polished templates and execution history). Only the error monitoring system is active, suggesting the platform may be in pre-launch or experiencing operational issues.

5. LIFECYCLE COMPLETENESS: The lottery winner journey shows gaps - we see notification delivery but no workflows for: lottery entry, Fair Queue selection, payment processing, ticket delivery, or handling expired purchase windows. Support workflows classify issues but don't show resolution tracking or follow-up automation.

systemLandscape.name: Gmail
systemLandscape.role: Primary communication channel for all customer interactions
systemLandscape.narrative: Gmail serves as FairTix's nervous system - every customer touchpoint flows through it. This centralization reveals a small team consolidating operations through a single communication hub, but creates a critical single point of failure.
systemLandscape.insight: If Gmail API fails or hits rate limits, 87.5% of automations break, halting customer communications

systemLandscape.name: Google Sheets
systemLandscape.role: Operational database for lottery winners and support tracking
systemLandscape.narrative: Sheets function as FairTix's operational database, revealing a startup choosing accessibility over scale. The pattern suggests rapid prototyping and business user empowerment over engineering-first architecture.
systemLandscape.insight: Database operations via Sheets API will hit scaling limits as lottery volume grows

systemLandscape.name: Anthropic Claude
systemLandscape.role: AI brain for customer support classification and response generation
systemLandscape.narrative: Claude powers all support automation, showing FairTix betting on AI to scale customer service without proportional headcount. The sophisticated prompts reveal deep investment in AI-first support strategy.
systemLandscape.insight: Complete support automation dependency on single AI provider - no fallback if API fails

systemLandscape.name: Google Docs
systemLandscape.role: Knowledge base storage for FAQ content
systemLandscape.narrative: Docs stores the FAQ knowledge base, indicating content management happens through familiar tools rather than specialized systems. This suggests a lean operation prioritizing speed over sophistication.
systemLandscape.insight: FAQ updates require manual Doc editing - no CMS or version control visible

systemLandscape.narrative: Payment processing is mentioned throughout support categories and lottery emails but has zero workflow presence. This gap reveals either manual payment handling or integration through different systems.
systemLandscape.insight: Critical revenue function with no automation visibility - major operational gap

systemLandscape.narrative: Ticket delivery follows payment but lacks workflow automation. This suggests either manual fulfillment or integration outside the n8n platform, creating operational opacity.
